source: The first real issue (31 Oct): ccp_machine_test issue #102, item fri-jsonl-lint, brief run 0.brief in /mnt/project-files/first-real-issue/harness/journal (pre-contract prompt). The input is that run's input; the repo is ccp_machine_test at b772aff, main when the item started.

expect: packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none
A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2
packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]

The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes
packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool

The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head

trap: Real repo facts: README.md says 'No tools yet: packages/ is empty, and npm test says so and passes', which the new tool makes false; the root npm test runs workspaces with --if-present, so a workspace without a test script passes silently; and the test workflow runs npm ci, which fails unless package-lock.json gains the new workspace (the merged PR #103 changed package-lock.json).
must_catch: The builder brief has the builder update package-lock.json for the new workspace (for example with npm install) so that npm ci, which the test workflow runs, still works.
The builder brief has the builder replace the root README's 'No tools yet' statement, not just add a line.

The verifier brief makes sure the jsonl-lint tests really run under the root npm test, so it would notice them being skipped (the root script uses --if-present): for example by reading the test count, or by breaking lint() and seeing a test fail.
The verifier check for line 6 reads GitHub at the PR head: the PR body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and the test workflow's run is green at that sha.
must_not: A PASS or FAIL condition stricter than its line, such as exact error message wording, a branch-name rule, a mutation test, or a limit on which files the PR may touch.
A check that passes a line by reading the diff or file names only, where the line asks for behaviour the program shows when run.
